title: برومت رفيق كرتوني من أغراضك
prompt:
Turn each portrait photo I upload into its own premium design poster. Output one image per photo — no multi-image collages.

Use a 3:4 vertical layout with a clear top/bottom split. Keep both zones roughly balanced in height, but never stretch or distort the original photo to force a ratio. Keep a clean, sharp horizontal boundary between the zones.

Top half: faithfully preserve the original photograph — identity, facial features, expression, hairstyle, pose, clothing, gestures, real objects, spatial relationships, natural lighting, and original color mood. Only apply slight premium photo grading and ultra-fine film grain. Do not redraw the person or change their identity.

Bottom half: place the same person as a high-fidelity photographic cutout on a simple solid-color field. The person must stay photoreal — never turn them into illustration or a cartoon character.

From the original photo, pick one real object already present and most closely related to the person (camera, drink cup, suitcase, fruit, book, or personal item) and turn it into the single personified cartoon companion. Keep the object's real shape, color, and recognizable features; add thick black rubber-hose limbs, oval eyes, white gloves, light halftone dots, and restrained retro animation print texture.

The cartoon object must not just sit beside the person — it needs clear spatial interaction (holding hands, handing something, cheers, hug, reacting, or walking together). Interaction should feel natural, playful, and instantly readable. Do not cover the face. Do not add a second cartoon character.

Extract the bottom background color from the photo or object; use a restrained limited palette and leave about 22%–30% continuous empty space. Avoid sticker walls, dense decoration, and complex scenes.

Generate a short English title from the photo, paired with the label “PHOTO PLAY 01” and one observational English line. Main title: larger hand-lettered type with a retro cartoon feel; supporting text clear and restrained, matching the object's print material.

Overall: an editorial poster where real photography and a retro object-cartoon coexist — light, humorous, smart, stylish — while keeping the emotion of a real travel photo.

Avoid: cartoonizing the person, multiple mascots, existing animation characters, brand logos, sticker clutter, face occlusion, bad hands, cheap templates, garbled text, author name, QR codes, and watermarks.
description: صورتك الحقيقية مع غرض يتحول لشخصية كرتونية تتفاعل معك. من @Hamburgerai

title: برومت طبق طبخ ومكوّنات
prompt:
Turn each local-cuisine photo I upload into its own premium “Ingredient Observation Travel Plate” editorial poster. Output one image per photo. Do not combine multiple photos, plates, or dishes in one artwork.

The input should clearly feature one complete plate or bowl with at least three separately recognizable components (staple, meat, seafood, egg, vegetables, herbs, nuts, pickles, sauce, or garnish).

Use a 3:4 vertical composition with a clear contrast between original food photography (top) and ingredient-observation drawing (bottom).

Top half (~45%–50%): faithfully keep the original photo — plate/bowl silhouette, ingredient counts, placement, area relationships, real textures, natural light, viewing angle, and original colors. Only slight indie food-magazine / travel-publication grading plus very thin film grain.

Do not replating, replace ingredients, move food, change portions, add garnish, or redraw the photo as illustration. Mild environmental crop for framing is OK if the full plate remains clearly readable.

Use a straight, clean, restrained horizontal boundary between zones; a very narrow warm paper strip is OK. No gradients, feathering, dissolves, or ingredients crossing the boundary.

Bottom half (~50%–55%): warm off-white or ivory natural drawing paper with visible fiber, grain, slight stains, and irregular surface.

Do not redraw the full plate in the same composition. Instead, deconstruct that same dish into a spacious paper observation record:
1. Choose 3–6 real, clearly identifiable components from the photo;
2. Draw one highly simplified but instantly recognizable miniature of the full plate/bowl, centered or slightly low;
3. The mini plate usually spans 28%–40% of the bottom width;
4. Pull selected ingredients out as separate gouache samples, cross-sections, leaves, clusters, sauce swatches, or structure sketches;
5. Vary scale and orientation into a loose, not-fully-symmetric observation around the mini plate;
6. Use thin slightly hesitant black ink lines, arrows, and numbers to map samples back to approximate plate positions;
7. Keep 35%–50% continuous off-white empty paper — do not pack arrows, text, and ingredients.

Bottom materials language (handmade culinary field notebook):
- matte opaque gouache
- restrained black ink contours
- dry brush gaps
- uneven pigment coverage
- visible paper grain
- imperfect hand-painted edges
- subtle pencil construction marks

Forms should be highly simplified yet keep the most recognizable color, silhouette, cut, and grain of each ingredient. Not photoreal copies, not cartoon food icons.

Palette must come from the photo: compress to 4–6 low-to-medium saturation ingredient colors. Background stays off-white, warm gray, or a very light photo-related tint. One warm accent (sauce, yolk, chili, fruit) is OK; avoid neon and high-saturation menu art colors.

Typography must be grounded in photo facts and usually include:
- a 1–3 word English dish title;
- a place + study code, e.g. “THAILAND / PLATE STUDY 01”;
- one 5–12 word English taste/ingredient observation;
- 3–6 short numbered labels, e.g. “01 RICE” “02 EGG” “03 HERBS”.

If an ingredient cannot be reliably identified, do not invent names — use RICE, NOODLES, GREENS, SAUCE, GRILLED ITEM, PICKLED ITEM.

Use narrow handwritten recipe lettering, old recipe type, or soft humanist sans; warm black, deep gray-brown, or a dark from the photo. Slight broken ink, paper tooth, and handmade irregularity are welcome.

Main title must stay readable at chat-preview size; numbers/labels can be smaller but not decorative hairlines. Keep text in one continuous blank area like notes on paper — not slick overlaid digital type.

Overall feel: a traveler tasting a local dish, then carefully taking it apart, observing, and recording it — restrained, warm, clear, handmade, with a touch of taste-memory / travel archive.

Hard avoids: no clear single-plate subject; full multi-dish tables; multi-plate collages; restaurant/chef as hero; invented ingredients; adding ingredients not in the photo; redrawing the full plate to scale; realistic menu illustration; dense nutrition infographics; cartoon food; slick vector icons; plastic 3D food; full-bleed busy backgrounds; excessive text; prices; brands; logos; author name; signature; date; QR; URL; social UI; garbled text; fake Chinese; watermarks.
description: صورة طبقك فوق، وتحته رسم ملاحظة لمكوّنات الوجبة بأسلوب سفر. من @Hamburgerai

title: برومت تصوير ميرش فاخر
prompt:
[BRAND NAME]
Act as a High-End CGI Product Photographer and 3D Render Artist
specializing in streetwear merch and limited-edition collectibles.

PHASE 1: CONCEPT & OBJECT

Create a photorealistic CGI product shot of a premium keychain set
suspended in mid-air against a neutral gradient studio background.
The keychain set consists of THREE elements connected to a single
polished silver carabiner clip with a gold-plated split ring:

ELEMENT 1 — ACRYLIC TAG:

A rectangular acrylic charm (approx. 4:9 ratio, rounded corners, 3mm thick).
Layered construction: clear gloss acrylic front panel over a [BRAND NAME]-colored
background insert. The background insert carries bold, condensed all-caps
typography — autonomously generate a short poetic or brand-relevant phrase
(4–8 words) that matches [BRAND NAME]'s tone of voice, set in a heavy
condensed grotesque typeface (Bebas Neue / Impact / custom bold). Include
[BRAND NAME]'s URL or tagline in small print at the bottom of the insert.
Micro-printed fine text fills the lower third as a design texture element.

ELEMENT 2 — OVAL MEDALLION CHARM:

A die-cut oval hoop/ring shape (donut silhouette, 40mm diameter) made from
tinted translucent acrylic or resin. Autonomously determine the iconic
brand color of [BRAND NAME] and apply it as the tint (deep saturated,
jewel-tone translucency — e.g., gold, cobalt, emerald, crimson).
The [BRAND NAME] wordmark is engraved or UV-printed in bold all-caps
along the inner curve of the ring. Add 1–2 small iconographic symbols
(logo mark, globe icon, cloud glyph) laser-engraved onto the face.
Subtle radial sun-ray pattern embossed on the surface.

ELEMENT 3 — HARDWARE:

Silver anodized aluminum carabiner with knurled locking barrel.
Gold-plated brass split ring (key ring loop) at the top.
All metal surfaces show micro-scratches and machining marks —
no perfect CGI plastic. Industrial precision aesthetic.

PHASE 2: MATERIAL & TEXTURE

Render all acrylic elements with full Ray Tracing and Subsurface
Scattering — light must visibly pass through the tinted acrylic
creating internal glow. Apply Fresnel reflection on acrylic edges.
Surface imperfections: hairline scratches, micro-dust particles,
smudge traces on the clear panel (subtle, editorial-level — not dirty).
Metal: PBR metallic workflow — anisotropic specular highlights on
the carabiner barrel, brushed finish on the ring.
Typography on acrylic must appear screen-printed or UV spot-coated —
slight ink texture, not floating.

PHASE 3: COMPOSITION & STAGING

Levitation shot: the entire keychain set hangs suspended from the
top of frame, centered with a 10–15 degree rotation to the right
(showing dimensionality). Nothing touches a surface — pure float.
Camera angle: slightly below eye-level looking up at ~5 degrees,
portrait orientation (4:5 ratio).
Depth of Field: focus plane centered on the oval medallion,
acrylic tag in sharp secondary focus, top hardware with micro
bokeh blur. Aperture equivalent: f/4.0.
Negative space: generous — object occupies 55% of frame.

PHASE 4: LIGHTING

Primary: large octabox soft key light, positioned top-right at
45 degrees — creates clean specular bloom on acrylic edges.
Secondary: subtle rim light from bottom-left, cool temperature
(5500K), separates the object from background.
Background: seamless gradient cyclorama — dark steel blue (#1a2535)
at top transitioning to pale silver-grey (#d0d8e0) at bottom.
No hard shadows cast. Global Illumination active.
Chromatic Aberration: micro-level, visible only on acrylic edges
(adds realism, prevents CGI-plastic look).
No lens flare. No neon. No HDR overblown highlights.

TECH SPECS

Render engine: Octane Render or Blender Cycles (path-traced)
Resolution: 4096 x 5120px (4:5 portrait)
Samples: 4096 minimum
Color profile: Adobe RGB, D65 white point
Post-processing: subtle film grain overlay (ISO 400 equivalent),
+5 clarity, -10 highlights, neutral color grade
Output mood: High-end streetwear lookbook / limited drop product page
Style references: Kith accessories, Highsnobiety product editorial,
Fragment Design merch photography
NEGATIVE: No white studio infinity cove. No flat lay. No hand holding
the product. No fake bokeh blur filters. No AI plastic sheen.
No floating text outside the object.

title: برومت موكب تيشرت
prompt:
[BRAND NAME]. Act as a High-End Editorial Fashion Photographer specializing in dark, cinematic merch and streetwear product campaigns.

PHASE 1: CONCEPT & OBJECT

Photograph a single premium heavyweight cotton T-shirt hanging
on a slim matte black clothing hanger. The hanger is suspended
from an industrial chrome pipe rail with a visible mechanical
clamp/hook fitting — the pipe enters the frame from the upper
right corner at a diagonal angle, partially cropped by the frame.

THE T-SHIRT:
Oversized unisex silhouette, heavyweight garment-dyed cotton
(320–380gsm equivalent). Color: autonomously determine the most
iconic or culturally resonant base color associated with
[BRAND NAME] — apply as a washed, slightly faded version
(not factory-fresh, not overly distressed — editorial vintage).
The shirt hangs with natural gravity drape — subtle wrinkles
at the torso, slight fabric pull at the shoulders from the hanger.
 NOT ironed flat. NOT pinned. Pure natural hang.

NECK LABEL:
A small woven white label visible inside the back collar,
folded slightly outward. The label reads "[BRAND NAME]"
in fine serif or script typeface — small, understated, luxury.

CHEST GRAPHIC:
Autonomously design a chest-centered screen-print graphic
that reflects [BRAND NAME]'s visual identity and cultural world.
The graphic must follow this construction logic:
- Style: Vintage varsity / retro sports circular badge OR
editorial script lettering — the aesthetic that best fits
[BRAND NAME]'s DNA
- Technique: Screen-print appearance — ink sits ON the fabric,
visible halftone texture at edges, slight cracking on the
darkest ink areas (authentic vintage wear)
- Color: 2–3 colors maximum. Autonomously determine the palette
based on [BRAND NAME]'s iconic colors + white outline/stroke
- Content: [BRAND NAME] wordmark or monogram rendered in the
chosen style. Add one short sub-line of text (4–6 words)
that captures [BRAND NAME]'s ethos or cultural reference
- Scale: Graphic occupies ~35–40% of the shirt's chest area

PHASE 2: LIGHTING

Single dominant key light: large softbox positioned front-left,
elevated at 40 degrees above subject — Rembrandt lighting logic.
This creates:
- Strong illumination on the LEFT side of the shirt
- The graphic/print fully lit and readable
- RIGHT side falls into deep natural shadow (no fill light)
- Hanger hardware catches a sharp specular highlight
Color temperature: 4200K — slightly warm, tungsten-adjacent.
No rim light. No background light. No lens flare.
The shadow IS the aesthetic — do not fight it.

Global Illumination: subtle bounce from the lit shirt face
back onto the immediate background only.

PHASE 3: BACKGROUND & ATMOSPHERE

Seamless cyclorama backdrop: deep, saturated single-color
gradient. Autonomously select the background color that creates
maximum dramatic contrast with [BRAND NAME]'s shirt color
while staying within a dark, moody palette — deep crimson,
oxblood, prussian blue, forest shadow, noir charcoal.
Vignette: strong radial darkening toward all four corners —
center is 30% brighter than edges. No texture. No grain on BG.
The background reads as infinite depth.

PHASE 4: COMPOSITION & CAMERA

Orientation: Portrait, 4:5 ratio.
Camera angle: Slightly below eye-level, looking up 8–12 degrees —
gives the garment presence and weight
Framing: T-shirt occupies 70–75% of frame. Bottom hem is
cropped slightly. Sleeve tips reach near frame edges.
Hanger pipe enters from upper-right, cropped at frame edge.
The hook/clamp mechanism is fully visible — it's a design element.
Rotation: Entire composition tilts 4–6 degrees counter-clockwise.
Depth of Field: f/5.6 equivalent — entire shirt in sharp focus,
background at soft focus threshold (not bokeh blurred —
just atmospheric depth). Macro detail on fabric weave visible.

TECH SPECS

Render/Capture style: Photorealistic — NOT CGI render aesthetic.
Must read as actual studio photography.
Fabric texture: Individual cotton weave threads visible on
the lit areas. Pilling micro-texture on surface. Subsurface
light interaction on thick fabric ridges.
Print texture: Screen-print ink layer has tactile presence —
slightly raised, edge halftone dots, micro-cracking in dark fills.
No AI plastic sheen on fabric. No oversaturated colors.
No symmetrical composition. No ghost mannequin. No flat lay.
Resolution: 4096 x 5120px. Post: Subtle film grain (ISO 800 equiv.), slight desaturation
(-8), lifted blacks (cinematic), neutral-warm color grade.
Style references: Undercover FW campaigns, Raf Simons archive
product shots, Stüssy × Our Legacy editorials, Highsnobiety
product features.
NEGATIVE: No model wearing the shirt. No white background.
No floating hanger (hardware must be attached to visible pipe).
No CGI fabric simulation. No overly bright studio look.

title: برومت إعلان مشروب غازي
prompt: Create a Cannes-level flagship advertising poster for an original soft drink brand named BUBBLENANA, featuring the hero product Banana Cream Sparkling Soda. Build the image with refined Orbit motion and clean Transit reduction, creating a bold, globally polished FMCG launch key visual. Core composition: Use a vertical poster with a seamless, fully saturated banana-yellow background, pure and uninterrupted. Keep the environment completely minimal so the product, mascot, and headline dominate with absolute clarity. Hero structure: At center-right, place a premium 3D anthropomorphic banana character in a dynamic forward-running pose, full of joyful momentum and clean silhouette appeal. The peel opens naturally into limbs, with believable volume and refined texture. The face should feel expressive, charming, and globally brandable, with premium character realism rather than a childish cartoon look. Product dominance: At center-left foreground, place one oversized hyper-realistic aluminum can of BUBBLENANA Banana Cream Sparkling Soda, held forward toward the camera by the banana mascot. The can must sit slightly closer to the viewer than the character, creating strong depth and clear commercial dominance. It should feel ice-cold, highly detailed, and premium, with crisp condensation droplets, elegant metallic reflections, and clean modern packaging hierarchy. Orbit structure: Use the composition to create a strong visual loop: curved headline -> mascot face -> presenting arm -> hero can -> lower body stride -> floating banana slices -> back up into the headline. Reinforce the orbit with the can tilt, the leg motion, the arc of the title, and the placement of a few restrained banana slices. The eye should always return to the can as the core brand anchor. Packaging direction: Design the can with a premium, globally publishable identity: BUBBLENANA, BANANA CREAM, SPARKLING SODA. Add only very restrained supporting details such as: "soft fizz", "serve chilled". Keep the front-of-pack clean, elegant, and easy to read. Avoid noisy claims. Typography system: At the upper center-right, place one large original curved headline in bold custom rounded display typography: "PEEL THE FIZZ". The headline should feel playful but polished, with premium spacing and clean outline control. Add one short supporting line in smaller refined type near the can: "Creamy sparkle. Pure lift." Keep typography minimal and internationally styled. Transit reduction: Remove all unnecessary copy, long descriptive text, and excessive social-style details. Keep only the essential brand-building elements: logo, headline, hero can, mascot, one short support line, and a small CTA. At the bottom center, place a tiny clean CTA capsule: "TASTE NOW". Nothing else should compete with the hero product. Floating elements: Use only 2-3 softly motion-blurred banana slices, placed sparingly to support the sense of movement and flavor. Keep them subtle and secondary.
